title: They Fixed the Streetlamp
status: concept-proposal (Creative Director, 2026-11-19; not approved; awaiting owner review)
hook_line: I reported the broken streetlamp. They fixed it.
first_visual: A dead streetlamp outside a window; under it, a shape darker than the night.

beats.visual: Dead streetlamp beyond Ivy's window; beneath it, a shape darker than the dark.
beats.vo: I reported the broken streetlamp. They fixed it.

beats.visual: Phone form: 'Lamp WL-14 not working' (UI overlay).
beats.vo: Three years outside my window. Dead.

beats.visual: Next night: the lamp blinks on, warm; Ivy smiles at the window.
In the cone, a tall figure stands beneath, face up toward the lamp.
beats.vo: And I saw what stood under it.

beats.visual: Flicker-cut through old dark nights; the darker shape in every one (re-graded clip 1).
Key moment: the figure slowly lowers its gaze from the lamp to Ivy's window; lamp eyes.
beats.vo: It had never been able to see me either.

beats.visual: Ivy slaps off her bedroom light.
Streetlamp clicks off; ping: 'Fault reported by resident. We're sending someone round.' Moth on the lamp.

ending: She kills her light, too late. The lamp clicks off. Ping: 'Fault reported by resident. We're sending someone round.'
loop_note: Yes. The final dark lamp equals frame 1, now with the knowledge of what stands beneath.

originality_review: Original and on-brand (light reveals both ways). It does not use the porch-light/door premise flagged in research; this is a public streetlamp and a mutual-sight twist.
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: Ivy reports the dead streetlamp outside her window. Fixed, its light reveals a tall figure that has stood beneath it every night. Now that the street is lit, it can see her too.

hooks.line: I reported the broken streetlamp. They fixed it.
hooks.first_visual: A dead streetlamp outside a window; under it, a shape darker than the night.

hooks.line: For three years I couldn't see what stood under it.
hooks.first_visual: A warm lamp cone flicking on over snow.

hooks.line: The lamp's fixed. Someone's standing under it.
hooks.first_visual: A tall figure in a pool of lamplight, face up.

hooks.line: The dark wasn't hiding it from me. It was hiding me.
hooks.first_visual: A figure lowering its gaze to a lit window.
A council-style form confirmation on a phone.

setting: Ivy's bedroom window over Winter Lane; streetlamp WL-14.
conflict: Ivy wants the street lit, and gets what she asked for.
escalation: The lamp comes on, the figure is revealed, flashback flickers show it was always there, and its gaze lowers.
reveal: The darkness had protected her: neither could see the other.
